messages:
emily: quick RFC follow-up: proposal to try an adaptive credit-bucketing proxy at the ingress layer. goal: cut memory + CPU of per-tenant float state while preserving fairness and abuse signal quality. comments? :mag_right:

raghav: hmm, bucketing reduces resolution. what's the model for bucket movement? i.e., how do tenants move up/down buckets without thrashing?

emily: plan is a leaky-integrator per-tenant counter but we materialize only buckets. tenants get a tentative score updated locally; we only promote/demote tenants across buckets when they cross band thresholds plus a cooldown timer. this avoids churning on micro-spikes.

li: sounds promising for scale. two concerns: (1) abuse detector may prefer continuous scores for ML features, (2) fairness scheduler needs deterministic ordering. how do buckets preserve ordering?

emily: ordering inside a bucket is best-effort; we keep a recent-activity timestamp for tiebreak. abuse model gets both bucket id and the raw local counter as telemetry (raw counter only emitted for canary groups). the idea: prod consumes bucket + activity rate; ML features can be backfilled with raw counters from sample windows.

sofia: can we define bucket boundaries? static vs adaptive? i prefer adaptive boundaries that expand/shrink with cluster load so buckets remain meaningful under load shifts.

emily: agreed — propose adaptive quantiles computed every minute from a sampling stream. bucket_size=8 by default, with dynamic pivot points.

raghav: operational failure modes? if quantile compute fails we need sane fallback. also what about cross-proxy consistency? two ingress proxies should not disagree violently about a tenant's bucket.

emily: fallback: if quantile calc fails, proxy falls back to last-known pivot values for 5m then to a conservative static set. cross-proxy: we use a lightweight epoched pivots push (small proto) every 30s; last-writer-wins and a short jitter on apply to avoid sync storms.

tom: perf tradeoffs: less memory, but extra CPU for quantile sampling and epoch pushes. do we have SLOs for that?

emily: initial budget: sampling threads limited to 0.5 CPU on each proxy, quantile window 60s, local aggregation only. can tune.

li: integration with KV cache and reuse patterns? buckets might penalize high reuse bursts unless we bias thresholds by recent cache-hit ratio. we should annotate tenants with reuse hints (cache-hit-rate) for bucket assignment.

emily: good call. will add cache-hit-rate as a second axis for bucketing heuristics. bucket = f(rate, hit_rate) but still materialized as single id for simplicity.

sofia: testing approach? I can run a matrix: steady-high reuse, short-fat bursts, long tail noisy. we should compare fairness metrics (95/99 latencies), admission variance, and ML detector AUC on attack cases.

emily: test plan noted. canary approach: stage 1 emit-only (no admission change) for 2w, stage 2 soft-admit where buckets influence admission probability but never fully deny, stage 3 full enforcement behind kill-switch. ops-bot create metric tag for canary?

infra-bot: tag `credit_bucket_canary=true` created for 14d. :white_check_mark:

raghav: what about billing/metrics fidelity? some dashboards expect per-tenant exact token counts. we'll need to keep raw counters for billing pipeline or sample to reconstruct.

emily: we'll keep a compact raw counter stream exported to the billing pipeline (sampled at 1:100 for cold tenants; full export for billable accounts). must ensure privacy controls preserved.

tom: runbook items: (1) pivot-push lag > 60s -> degrade to static pivots (2) sampling CPU > budget -> reduce sample rate (3) many tenants demoted -> alert imbalance. Add diagnostic dashboards: pivot stability, bucket churn, sample-residuals.

emily: added to doc. deliverables: 1) lightweight proxy shim implementing sample -> pivot compute -> bucket assign + epoch push; 2) telemetry export hooks (bucket id, sample counters, cache-hit-rate); 3) canary plan + eval harness.

li: timeline?

emily: 1w prototype emit-only; 3w internal canary; 6w soft-admit; iterate based on metrics.

sofia: one more thought: ensure ML abuse model retraining includes bucketed features and we run ablation to ensure no regression. I'll own the evaluation and training replay.

emily: great. thanks all. i'll open a short RFC appendix with config knobs (bucket_count, cooldown_ms, pivot_window_ms, sample_rate) and invite people to comment. :sparkles:
